title: The one tour with the band and being fired as spokesman
summary: Touring was enough for him: he spoke for the men's pay demand and was replaced, with only nothing-to-speak-of recordings.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now, when Cab or Duke came back, then what happened?
Then they was out of work. That's when I'd go back to Russell or anybody else I could find to go to.
In other words, the Mills Blue Rhythm Band really didn't tour.
Well, they toured... They made a tour with me one time. I made a tour with them.
Yeah, we made a tour. And one was enough. I got fired and didn't come back!
Well, would you care to relate that little experience of how you became spokesman for the...?

Well...it's not a nice thing to repeat. There are things you don't brag about. But while we was on the road we was drawin' big crowds and one thing and another, and everybody thought we should get more money. Everybody but me. It didn't make no difference to me. As long as I was getting paid, I was satisfied. But everybody wanted more money.

So they cut the trip short, and Mills brought the band into New York. And we all got together, and he wanted to know what was the trouble. So it looked like nobody wanted to speak up about the money, so I opened my mouth -- and I was about one of the least interested parties in getting anything; I had never spoken up for no money or anything. I spoke up, I opened my mouth, thinking somebody else would back me up. And I told him, I said, 'Well, the men don't think we're getting paid enough.'

So Mr. Mills looked at me. 'Anybody else got anything to say?' Nobody said a word. So Mr. Mills said, 'Well, we'll replace Holmes, and the rest of the schedule will go down.' And there I am sittin' like a fool. And that was it. What was there to do after that? I come out the band; that was it. That's the reason I got out of it.
Well, you made a few recordings with the band.
